name: OnePlus 2
summary: ztOS on the OnePlus 2 (Snapdragon 810, MSM8994), on mainline Linux 7.3 with its own device tree and patches. The display, touch, hardware GPU (Adreno 430, OpenGL ES 3.0 on freedreno), Wi-Fi, Bluetooth with audio, battery, the modem (LTE, SMS, ringing and answering calls) and the loudspeaker work. There is no mobile data, no earpiece, microphones or call audio, no cameras, and the four A57 cores and CPU frequency scaling are not done, so it is an early port and not yet a usable phone. Tried on one OnePlus 2 (A2003); started from RAM with fastboot.
specs: 4× Cortex-A57 + 4× Cortex-A53 (A57 not brought up yet; the A53 run at a fixed 1.5 GHz)
github.com/luvingiane/oneplus2-mainline (kernel, device tree, patches, tools; a ztOS device layer is not written yet)

install.markdown:
> **This is not installable as a system yet.** The port boots ztOS from RAM with `fastboot boot` and runs it from the phone's userdata partition; there is no installer and no device layer in ztOS yet. Kernel, device tree, patches, initramfs and the build scripts are in [oneplus2-mainline](https://github.com/luvingiane/oneplus2-mainline) (see its README for the build and the status table).
>
> **Tried on one OnePlus 2 (A2003)** with an unlocked bootloader. Never flash the modem or bootloader partitions.

notes.title: Why the A57 cores are off
notes.text: With the four A57 cores on, the boot becomes intermittent (3 starts out of 4). The four A53 cores run at a fixed clock of about 1.5 GHz; CPU frequency scaling is still a draft.

notes.title: Airplane mode stops the modem
notes.text: On this phone AT+CFUN=4 crashes the modem firmware while it is registered, so airplane mode stops and restarts the modem instead.
